name: Autonomous Evaluation and Refinement of Digital Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Compares automatic trajectory evaluators for web navigation and device control against oracle judgments. The resulting feedback is used for agent fine-tuning and inference-time guidance, including experiments on WebArena.

name: From Novice to Expert: LLM Agent Policy Optimization via Step-wise Reinforcement Learning
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available for this review. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. Official full-paper experimental sections explicitly evaluate WebShop and Mind2Web; the overall optimization method also covers embodied and question-answering tasks.
summary: Introduces StepAgent, which compares agent and expert actions to supply intermediate rewards for policy learning, with implicit-reward and inverse-RL variants. Evaluation includes WebShop and Mind2Web alongside non-web tasks.

name: Guiding VLM Agents with Process Rewards at Inference Time for GUI Navigation
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Guides visual GUI agents at inference time with a process-reward model that evaluates intermediate actions. It combines stepwise guidance with trajectory reflection and retry mechanisms in static and interactive navigation tasks.

name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.

name: GUI-G$^2$: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-G2 replaces binary grounding rewards with Gaussian point rewards and spatial-coverage rewards. An adaptive variance tied to element dimensions supplies continuous training feedback for targets of different sizes, evaluated on the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

name: CRAFT-GUI: Curriculum-Reinforced Agent For GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CRAFT-GUI organizes GUI trajectories by difficulty for curriculum-based GRPO training. Its reward combines rule-based signals with model judgments, with evaluation on Android Control and an internal online benchmark.

name: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.

name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.

name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.

name: Scaling Agents for Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Behavior Judge, which converts execution trajectories into behavior narratives and compares multiple candidate rollouts. Experiments examine this selection approach on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AndroidWorld.

name: WebSTAR: Scalable Data Synthesis for Computer Use Agents with Step-Level Filtering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a pipeline that filters individual steps from noisy computer-agent rollouts and augments them with reasoning for training. WebSTAR and WebSCORE support GUI-policy supervision and a distilled process reward model, StepRM.

name: Step-GUI Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.

name: OS-Oracle: A Comprehensive Framework for Cross-Platform GUI Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OS-Oracle synthesizes GUI critic examples and trains a pre-action critic with supervised learning followed by consistency-preserving GRPO. It introduces OS-Critic Bench across mobile, web, and desktop settings and tests critic-assisted agents in OSWorld and AndroidWorld.

name: EchoTrail-GUI: Building Actionable Memory for GUI Agents via Critic-Guided Self-Exploration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: EchoTrail-GUI builds a memory of successful GUI trajectories through autonomous exploration filtered by a reward model. It retrieves relevant trajectories as in-context guidance for new tasks and evaluates the approach on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.

name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.

name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.

name: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ADMIRE extracts milestones from successful GUI explorations to provide adaptive intermediate rewards. It assigns credit differently to successful and failed trajectories and evaluates training on AndroidWorld, with additional transfer studies in web and embodied settings.

name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.

name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.

name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.

name: Android Coach: Improve Online Agentic Training Efficiency with Single State Multiple Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Android Coach, which uses a learned critic to evaluate multiple candidate actions at each observed emulator state. Process rewards and a group-wise advantage estimator support online training, evaluated on AndroidLab and AndroidWorld.

name: AJ-Bench: Benchmarking Agent-as-a-Judge for Environment-Aware Evaluation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: AJ-Bench evaluates judge agents that actively gather evidence from search, data systems and graphical interfaces. Its annotated tasks and trajectories test information acquisition, state verification and process verification.

name: StainFlow: Entity-Stain Tracking and Evidence Linking for Process Rewards in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: StainFlow tracks visually verifiable task entities through GUI trajectories to identify phases and retrieve focused evidence windows. Its process-reward model is tested for both online policy learning and trajectory-completion judgments.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: Reinforcement Learning for Computer-Use Agents with Autonomous Evaluation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: The framework uses a vision-language judge’s final-screen assessment as a terminal reward for GUI reinforcement learning. It models evaluator noise and corrects the reward estimator used by PPO across desktop benchmarks.

name: VisCritic: Visual State Comparison as Process Reward for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: VisCritic compares before/after screenshots through change-aware visual features and an action-conditioned critic. Weakly supervised samples from existing traces train judgments of action success, progress and error type for GUI-agent verification.

name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.

name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.

name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.

name: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: StepReflect predicts structured per-action reflections from transition specifications and paired visual evidence. The paper distinguishes offline transition-label accuracy from online task success when the reflection model is integrated into mobile agents.

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.

name: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GSAR, which synthesizes GUI tasks and successful goal states, then annotates task-relevant interface elements as reward anchors. These anchors support offline trajectory verification and online policy training.

name: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces AdaptRubric, which retrieves reusable criteria for a GUI task family and then generates instruction-specific checks for concrete values and constraints. It evaluates these adaptive rubrics in offline reward assessment and online agent optimization.

name: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experiments, reported performance and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains discriminative web world models to distinguish the true next state from outcomes of alternative actions. Branching web trajectories support training, followed by tests of predicted-state matching, process-reward action ranking and end-to-end WebArena-Lite selection.

name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SURFPRM, which turns web demonstrations into an interaction-element graph for synthesizing grounded negative actions. Its contrastive preference data trains process reward models to distinguish plausible on-page alternatives and guide downstream trajectory search.

name: VeriCUA: Learning Proactive Verification for Reliable GUI Agent Rewards
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 method/evaluation sections. The Judge is trained on OSWorld and frozen for MobileWorld/WebArena transfer; downstream Actor RL is separate. Evaluation uses screened terminal outcomes, and reported cost counts Probe tokens. No independent reproduction.
summary: VeriCUA trains a Judge to select verification checks and stopping decisions while a frozen Probe inspects the post-task GUI. Single-attempt reinforcement learning balances verdict correctness and Probe use.
